newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-British drug stocks surge to record highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-British drug stocks surge to record highs.

text.p: Shares in Britain's top three drug companies leapt to to record highs on Tuesday amid a renewed surge in demand from investors on both sides of the Atlantic, dealers and analysts said.
Spurred by gains in the shares in New York on Monday as the Dow rose to record highs, Glaxo Wellcome Plc gained 31-1/2pence to 12.43 pounds by 1430 GMT -- after reaching a record 12.82 pounds.
SmithKline Beecham Plc climbed 34p to 10.76 pounds after hitting a peak of 11.08, and Zeneca Group Plc was up 25-1/2p at 1,968-1/2 after reaching a high of 20.00 pounds.
The sector's advance helped power the FTSE 100 index to a record 4,720.3 in late morning on Tuesday, up 60.7 points on the day.
"We have just seen loads and loads of buyers," said one market-maker in drug stocks at a leading investment bank in London, "investors seem to love the sector, I think it is a bit of herd instinct."
Analysts said the drug sector could be in demand because of long-term positive factors, highlighted by recent hopes in the U.S. that inflation was unlikely to pick up in the near future.

"In a low inflation environment, what you want to be invested in is a sector with solid (profits) momentum, and you can't do better in that respect than the pharmaceuticals," said Peter Cartwright, analyst at brokerage Williams de Broe.
"And as the economy gets richer and older, you can't do better than the pharmaceuticals."

Cartwright also highlighted a report in Business Week magazine that death rates for AIDS patients were plummeting under the impact of combination drug therapies -- expanding the market for anti-AIDS drugs where Glaxo in particular is a leader.
Patients living longer create a potentially lucrative market for expensive AIDS therapies -- which Business Week said can cost as much as $15,000 a year per patient.

Other analysts said the British drug sector was being re-rated to bring it in line with international peers, and that there was a growing enthusiasm among U.S. investors for European stocks amid nervousness over the ratings on some U.S. stocks.
BZW analyst Steve Plag said the drug sector was being re-rated worldwide.
"There has been a general realisation over the past 12 months that the industry has undergone a fundamental change in its technology base and a sea change in productivity," Plag said.

He said that with U.S. and UK economic growth also looking less certain, drug firms were benefitting from their defensive appeal -- in that their profits are relatively immune from swings in the economic cycle.

Separately, analysts at NatWest Markets were said to have made positive comments on growth prospects at SmithKline on Tuesday following a meeting with executives from the company, but they continued to rate the stock a "hold" because of its high market valuation.
"NatWest is talking about 15 percent earnings growth and there are no U.S. patent expiries until after the year 2000," said one dealer. "Good earnings growth will sustain it into the next century."
